documents.title: Artificial Intelligence Policy
documents.stance_why: The policy does not ban or require AI. It welcomes responsible use ('encouraged to use these tools responsibly') but leaves academic use to instructors: 'Students using AI must follow individual instructors’ expectations outlined in teaching materials' and 'Course syllabi will provide course-specific expectations'. So the stance is delegates.
documents.summary: A university-wide policy from the Provost covering teaching, research and administration. It sets principles on verification, data protection, disclosure and ethics, assigns governance duties, and leaves classroom AI rules to each instructor's syllabus.

units.why: The policy statement says the community is "encouraged to use these tools responsibly", a general welcoming default that is not tied to any single course; P02 fits because it allows and encourages use, with conditions.
units.anchor: community is encouraged to use these tools responsibly

units.why: This sentence states the policy purpose: general guidance so AU can leverage AI while meeting legal and ethical duties. An institution-level framework statement is P56.
units.anchor: intent of this policy is to provide general guidance on the use of AI

units.why: The policy "establishes a framework for responsible, ethical, transparent, and appropriate AI use", which is a framework and principles statement (P56).
units.anchor: establishes a framework for responsible, ethical, transparent, and appropriate AI use

units.why: Scope sentence: the policy covers faculty, staff and students and "teaching, learning, research, administrative functions, and scholarly communication". It sets what the policy covers, so P61 rather than P56.
units.anchor: applies to all faculty, staff, and students at the university and governs

units.why: The definition of Generative AI, including tools "embedded in other software", sets what the policy covers; P61 definitions. The embedded-software clause could suggest P07 but nothing here is a rule about editors or IDEs.
units.anchor: offerings that are embedded in other software
units.frag_end: text and images, whereas traditional AI

units.why: The AI Agent definition ("a system that uses artificial intelligence to autonomously perceive its environment") fixes a policy term, so P61.
units.anchor: An AI agent is a system that uses artificial intelligence to autonomously perceive its environment
units.frag_end: without human intervention at each step.

units.why: Users are "responsible for verifying the accuracy of AI -generated information" and reviewing for bias or hallucinations; this is verify-output (P31).
units.anchor: Users are responsible for verifying the accuracy of AI -generated information

units.why: Users "must comply with copyright and intellectual property laws"; the rule is about legal limits on AI content, so P52.
units.anchor: users must comply with copyright and intellectual property laws, avoid infringement

units.why: "AI -generated content should be viewed as a starting point, not the finished product" and must be "thoroughly reviewed"; it asks users to check the result, so P31 (verify).
units.anchor: All AI-generated content must be thoroughly reviewed

units.why: "must never be put into an open AI system": confidential and sensitive data is barred from open tools, which is P50 (protect data) rather than P49 since it concerns data generally, not course materials.
units.anchor: must never be put into an open AI system

units.why: AU login credentials "must not be provided to, or shared with, AI Agents without written authorization from the CIO"; a security rule on agents and data, fitting P50 best.
units.anchor: AU login credentials must not be provided to, or shared with, AI Agents

units.why: "The use of an AI system must be disclosed to capture institutional knowledge"; a general duty to disclose AI use, so P24.
units.anchor: The use of an AI system must be disclosed to capture institutional knowledge

units.why: Code that is AI-derived must be documented as to "which code section is AI -derived and who reviewed it", i.e. marked where it is used (P27).
units.anchor: there must be documentation as to which code section is AI -derived
units.frag_start: For example, if AI is used

units.why: "Disclosure should be considered when using AI in much the same way as citing a source in writing" frames disclosure as citation; P45 treats AI like an outside source under existing citation rules, a closer fit than P24 here.
units.anchor: using AI in much the same way as citing a source

units.why: Use must "comply with any terms of use or contractual limitations"; this concerns terms of use of AI tools, P52.
units.anchor: must comply with any terms of use or contractual limitations
units.frag_start: The use of an AI system must comply

units.why: Users "should have all terms or use or contracts for AI systems reviewed by the Legal Department"; a review of AI contracts, P65.
units.anchor: Users should have all terms or use or contracts for AI systems reviewed
units.frag_end: contractual obligations in using an AI system.

units.why: Data privacy laws and informed consent for human data: "accessing AU data with or without authorization does not imply permission to use that data in AI models" restricts AI data use, P50.
units.anchor: does not imply permission to use that data in AI models
units.frag_end: use that data in AI models.

units.anchor: safeguard the rights and privacy of human participants

units.why: "Personally identifiable information must be protected" and data must be managed per privacy policies; P50.
units.anchor: Personally identifiable information must be protected

units.anchor: Users should explain how AI is used in decision- making

units.anchor: AI should not replace human- centered approaches or be used for automated decisions

units.anchor: must clearly disclose the involvement of AI in the content creation process

units.anchor: Faculty, staff, and volunteers will be provided with AI literacy guidance

documents.stance_why: AI appears as misconduct unless permitted: cheating includes devices 'including use of AI text generators' without instructor permission, and 'Students should not submit texts generated in part or full by artificial intelligence unless the instructor has granted explicit permission'.
